# Code review — September 13, 2026

Review focused on the current-directory header, shared help/exit banner, recent API-key restart guidance, and command authorization, execution, and redaction boundaries. This is not a complete audit of every repository component. All four findings were subsequently corrected; the original descriptions below document the reviewed baseline.

Credential examples use synthetic strings only. The redaction findings were reproduced through the compiled application redactor without network requests or changes to real credentials. The authentication findings follow the application error branches and environment precedence. Existing unrelated working-tree changes were preserved.

## Resolution

| Finding | Implemented correction | Regression coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Credential field names | Share `CredentialFieldPolicy` across text and structural audit redaction; decode JSON names and redact complete credential values while preserving typed metadata and duplicate properties. | `CredentialFieldPolicyTests`, `AuditCredentialFieldTests`, `SensitiveDataStructureRegressionTests`, `PrivacyFlowRegressionTests` |
| 2. Quoted or truncated values | Scan PowerShell doubled quotes, backticks, concatenated scalar segments, here-strings, serialized JSON, and incomplete quoted values through their full boundary. | `CredentialValueRegressionTests`, `SensitiveDataStructureRegressionTests`, `AuthorizedCommandWorkflowTests.RunAsync_ReviewedCredentialFormats_PreservesLocalPreviewAndRedactsPersistence` |
| 3. Admin-key authentication hint | Route explicit organization-cost warnings through the common error formatter, keeping cached costs available. | `ApplicationErrorTests.RunAsync_CostRefreshFailure_RendersExpectedWarningAndCachedCosts` (401 and 503) |
| 4. Stale parent environment guidance | Translate full terminal-application/IDE restart guidance in all six languages and explain that the current `hm` process already has the updated key. | `ApplicationErrorTests`, `LocalizationTests`; README and privacy guidance updated |

Additional regression checks protect redaction idempotence, suffixes attached to placeholders, numeric-prefixed credential variables, recognizable secrets in JSON property names, safe adjacent data, and exact local command/output previews. The provider integration tests capture synthetic HTTP requests in memory and check actual SQLite persistence plus typed token accounting. No real provider requests or credentials are used.

The final focused review found no remaining blocker in the four findings or the additional regressions identified while implementing their fixes. This does not claim exhaustive detection of arbitrary confidential text or evaluation of arbitrary PowerShell expressions.

Validation completed: preflight, restore, formatting verification, XML method comments, Release build with zero warnings/errors, 320/320 automated tests, and eight isolated CLI smoke checks. Test execution was already underway when the concurrent repository rule requiring an explicit request for tests was discovered; no further test runs followed.

## Original findings (resolved)

### 1. [P1] Common credential fields survive redaction

`PromptMeUp/Services/SensitiveDataRedactor.cs:71` recognizes underscore-delimited token names but misses common JSON fields such as `accessToken`, `SecretAccessKey`, and `SessionToken`. The structural audit filter in `PromptMeUp/Services/ActivityAuditService.cs:182` also misses these names.

Both synthetic examples pass through `SensitiveDataRedactor.Redact` unchanged:

```json
{"accessToken":"synthetic-access-value","tokenType":"Bearer"}
{"Credentials":{"SecretAccessKey":"synthetic-secret-value","SessionToken":"synthetic-session-value"}}
```

`AuthorizedCommandWorkflow` uses this redactor for captured output before audit persistence and AI follow-up. Consequently recognizable credential fields in authorized command output can reach SQLite and the provider. Normalize credential property names consistently across the text and structural filters, covering common token/key fields while preserving usage counters.

### 2. [P1] PowerShell quoting and incomplete quoted values expose secret suffixes

The value alternatives in `PromptMeUp/Services/SensitiveDataRedactor.cs:71` handle backslash escaping but do not fully handle PowerShell quoting. For example:

```text
Input:  PASSWORD='synthetic''tail'; safe=keep
Output: PASSWORD='[redacted-credential]''tail'; safe=keep
```

Backtick-escaped double quotes similarly leave a suffix visible. An incomplete quoted value such as `password="synthetic head tail` leaves `head tail` after redaction; output truncation can create this condition. These remnants can persist or become provider input through the same command-output and follow-up paths. Handle doubled single quotes, backtick escapes, and incomplete quoted values explicitly while retaining the exact local preview.

### 3. [P2] Organization-cost authentication errors omit restart guidance

`PromptMeUp/Application/PromptMeUpApplication.cs`, in `TryRefreshPricingAsync`, renders `exception.Message` directly for an explicit costs refresh. This bypasses `FormatErrorMessage` for HTTP 401 errors from `OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY`. After replacing that key in setup, `hm --costs` launched from a stale terminal can fail without the restart hint. Route this warning through the same authentication-message formatter.

### 4. [P2] A new shell session can still inherit the stale key

`Setup.KeyRestartRequired` and `Error.KeyRestartRequired` in `PromptMeUp/Services/FeatureText.cs` suggest that opening a new session activates a saved key. A nested `pwsh` launched from the existing shell inherits its old process environment; a new integrated terminal can likewise inherit an IDE's stale environment. `EnvironmentSecretService.Load` still prioritizes that value over the saved user variable. Tell the user to fully close and reopen the terminal application, including its IDE host when applicable, or provide explicit environment-refresh instructions.

## UI review

No actionable new defect was found in the current-directory and banner changes. The orchestrator supplies the directory to the passive view, and Spectre markup is escaped. `RenderProjectBanner` is shared by help and process exit and renders once per invocation. The banner's output remains available after input cancellation. Automated rendering checks cover narrow terminals, emoji options, literal bracketed paths, and help/exit deduplication.

The existing detached-descendant process limitation is already documented in the September 2 review and is not reported as a new finding here. No native Linux/macOS run or real provider authentication test was performed during this review.
